title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC0LB, and what is open
description: Proof status of the six-state machine 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE---: what is proved in Lean, what is computed, what is only observed.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape. This page tracks what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

The machine is set up in Lean on the shared library and simulated in Python and C. The tape is made of pairs 10 in blocks separated by single cells; sweeps to the right and to the left shift the pairs by one cell, and a sweep to the right marks each block boundary it crosses. Lean proves the halting shape, the sweep rules, and that the right end of the tape is a base-3 counter: each trip of the head from the right end and back subtracts one from a number written in the separator cells, moving one pair between two blocks of each level it changes. What is not proved is the top of the counter, where a borrow reaches the irregular blocks at the left end; there the run looks like a recursion on long blocks (walls) in front of which the left end repeats the run from blank tape. The explainer runs the machine and the counter in the browser.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 20,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 steps with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1010 steps. These are floors, not the way to an answer.

Where a halt would come from. The only halting transition is F reading 1. Lean proves that in the run from blank tape every halt comes two steps after the head, in state E, reads 0 1 1. A sweep to the right in E crosses each block boundary 0 10 by marking it 0 11; so the machine halts exactly if a sweep in E meets a mark that an earlier sweep left and nothing has cleared, in step with E's pairs. Whether that can happen is the question. Lean proves that no trip of the right-end counter halts (section on the counter below), so a halt can only come from the top of the counter, the trips that reach the left end.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly in state F reading a 1, and E>0 1 1 halts after two more ordinary steps, whatever the rest of the tape.

claims.title: Every halt comes from E reading 0 1 1
claims.text: F is entered from A or D reading 1 and then reads the cell to their right. D is entered only by C1 → 0LD, which leaves a 0 to D's right, so the D route never halts (d_right_zero); A is entered only by E0 → 0RA. So in the run from blank tape every halt happens two ordinary steps after a configuration E>0 1 1, and the machine halts from blank tape only if E>0 1 1 occurs.

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: E runs right over any number of pairs 10, shifting each one cell to the right, 2 steps a pair (e_run). E at a block boundary 0 10 turns it into 0 11 in 3 steps and goes on (e_mark). B runs left over pairs two at a time, shifting each one cell to the right, 4 steps per two pairs, through D in between (b_run). All three hold for every number of pairs and any tape around them; the proofs were written by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py from symbolic runs.

claims.title: The right end is a base-3 counter
claims.text: When the head is back at the right end (state C reading the 0 of 0 10, blank beyond), read the tape from the right as levels s (10)^g s′ (10)^W, with digit 2 for seps 1 1, 1 for 0 1 and 0 for 0 0. The machine returns to the right end after subtracting one from the base-3 number the digits spell (last level lowest): a digit 2 becomes 1 (s → 0, one pair from W to g), a digit 1 becomes 0 (s′ → 0), and each digit 0 passed by the borrow becomes 2 (one pair from W to g), except that the last level's W grows, by 1 or 2. Proved for every block length (g, W odd for digit 2, even otherwise, W at least 1 to 4 pairs), any number of borrows and any tape left of the level where the trip turns, so no such trip halts. The proofs chain eight symbolic pieces of the run, generated by symtm.py, by induction on the number of borrows.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 20,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel. At step 18 the tape is 1 0 1 0 1 0 1 F>0 (blank_at_18).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000,000 steps
claims.text: The same run for 10<sup>7</sup> steps, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c (tested against the Python reference simulator) runs 1010 steps from blank tape without a halt, in under a minute. At that point 258,671 cells are visited and 129,335 of them are 1.

claims.title: Almost every trip in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps is a counter step
claims.text: Of the 151,240 trips from the right end and back in the first 1011 steps, 150,680 are covered by the counter theorems and all end as they say. The other 560 are the top of the counter: 321 borrow past the levels into the irregular blocks at the left end, and 239 meet one of the leftmost few levels when it is too short or of the wrong parity for the theorems. Run with the macro simulator tools/py/bbtools/macro.py (blocks of 4 cells, runs crossed at once; tested cell for cell against the reference simulator), 1011 steps in about two minutes.
claims.where: python3 py/counter.py check 1e11; tests/test_machine.py checks the first 108 steps

claims.title: No simple conserved quantity
claims.text: No quantity a·(number of 1s) + b·(head position) + W[state] is conserved modulo m for any m from 2 to 12, so no such count rules out halting candidates, unlike the mod-3 invariant of the holdout.

claims.title: Windows of cells do not separate the halt
claims.text: Closed tape languages built from windows of 2 to 7 cells (tools/py/bbtools/ctl.py) all cover the run and all still allow a halt, so they prove nothing here. The protection seems to be the alignment of the pairs 10 with E's sweep, which windows of raw cells do not record.

claims.title: The tape is blocks of pairs, and grows like the square root of time
claims.text: Each time the head reaches a new cell at the left end, the tape reads 0 0 (10)^n1 0 (10)^n2 … 0 (10)^nk 1, sometimes with a word 110 right after a block. Through 1010 steps the width is about 2.6√t at step t and half of the cells are 1. The head goes back and forth between the right end and the block boundaries; each sweep to the right in E marks the boundaries, and each excursion from the right end runs left to a boundary and back.

claims.title: A mark never sits after a boundary at the left-end moments
claims.text: In all 207 left-end moments up to 1010 steps, the word 110 occurs 67 times, always right after a block of pairs and never right after a boundary 0. Right after a pair it is out of step with E's sweep (E arrives on its first 1 and turns), so it is harmless; right after a boundary it would be the halting shape.

claims.title: In front of a long block, the left end replays the run from blank tape
claims.text: When the tape at a left-end moment starts 0 0 (10)^W 0 with W large (a wall), the following left-end moments repeat those of the run from blank tape, the blank run's last block replaced by the wall, and the wall shrinks by the same amounts every time: 1, 3, 2, 4, 2, 10, 6, 10, 6, 2, 6, 12, … whether W is 71, 257, 1,547 or 43,801. The first wall, 257 pairs at step 277,787, is followed by 29 replayed moments. Walls nest (at step 1.8·109 the tape starts with walls of 1,768 and 10,762 pairs), so the run looks like a recursive counter. The count of replayed moments is a lower bound: the moments are taken where the head extends the tape on the left after extending it on the right, which the replay need not keep in step.

claims.title: The top of the counter
claims.text: The trips that the counter theorems do not cover, as maps on the block lengths: a borrow that reaches the left end (how a new level or wall is made), a level that runs short, the wall replay of the blank run, and whether any of them can leave a mark right after a boundary in E's way.

check: bb6-1RB1RF_1LC0LB/lean/check.sh               # the library, then Machine, Blank, Rules, Counter, Axioms
python3 bb6-1RB1RF_1LC0LB/py/counter.py check 1e10    # trips of the right-end counter; levels / events
gcc -O2 -o tokrun tools/c/tokrun.c && ./tokrun 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE--- 10000000000 a=10,b=110 L 1000 > left.txt && python3 bb6-1RB1RF_1LC0LB/py/replay.py left.txt
